events.summary: Pentecostal Church donated five million rupees to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka fund.
India announced AYUSH scholarships covering tuition and student allowances for Sri Lankan applicants.
Customs scheduled launch of cargo tracking and electronic payment services.
Plantation companies agreed to provide land for homes for cyclone-displaced estate residents.
Treasury allocated 500 million rupees for rebuilding cyclone damage without raising public taxes.
President directed officials to expedite establishing a Central Highlands protection authority.
PUCSL opened public consultation on proposed electricity tariff revisions.
Treasury announced a government subsidy for electricity consumers.
Funding was allocated for restoration of Mannar Dutch Fort.
Authorities began steps to recover contractors’ duplicate payments after an interbank transfer error.
Cabinet approved interim homes for 1,000 families displaced by Cyclone Ditwah.
Officials considered feasibility studies for cable cars and improvements to wildlife sanctuary visitor facilities.
Authorities began investigating a reported missing payment to the US Postal Service.
The Treasury reportedly paid cybercriminals; a special investigation began.
Airport and wildlife authorities signed an agreement to establish a wildlife office at Mattala airport.
The local council proposed camera monitoring and legal action against dumping at the bird sanctuary.
PET scan examinations stopped at government hospitals because required radiopharmaceutical supplies ran out.
Batticaloa Municipal Council opened a newly built beach promenade.
Health Ministry provided two advanced medical machines to Kandy National Hospital.
National digital calendar for cultural, sports and business events officially launched.
Norway agreed to provide satellite technology assistance and specialised training for fisheries monitoring.
Treasury appointed a special committee as investigations into the misdirected debt payment continued.
President ordered payment of compensation to eligible homes damaged by Cyclone Ditwah by May-end.
President directed officials to identify sites for temporary housing for displaced residents.
Police officers donated one day’s salaries to the Rebuilding Sri Lanka Fund.
China’s donation of 2026 school-uniform fabric was officially confirmed as complete.
Cabinet approved the proposal to proceed with consultancy procurement for the extension study.
Low-floor bus service for passengers with disabilities launched at Makumbura.
Government set May 27 to June 2 as Vesak Week, with national celebrations and a state festival.
The 2026 budget allocated compensation for farmers affected by the Nilwala River saltwater barrier.
The government announced the fuel QR-code distribution system will continue indefinitely.
Ministry began a Clean Sri Lanka pilot with ten accessible low-floor buses from Makumbura.
Government reported progress on its planned network of 1,000 health and wellness centres.
Police announced special traffic arrangements for the Indian vice-president’s Colombo visit.
Fuel QR-code distribution resumed after a temporary holiday-period exemption.
ADB-funded permanent desalination plant expansion is being developed for Neduntivu.
Card fare payment preparations are complete for all Sri Lanka Transport Board buses.
Charities urged the government to provide permanent homes to people displaced by Cyclone Ditwah.
Petroleum Corporation reinstated QR-code fuel distribution from midnight Saturday.
Nallur council set up temporary drinking-water tanks and shade for residents in Jaffna.
Education Ministry said Grade 1 curriculum reforms are continuing, with activity books being distributed.
Registration of Persons Department public services were suspended for one day after a computer failure.
Applications opened for the 2026 President’s Environmental Awards, with awards planned for October.
A cyclone-damaged home was rebuilt under the government compensation programme in Kalnawa.
NBRO introduced a risk-based scheme to prioritize compensation for cyclone-damaged homes and businesses.
A new bus service began serving Lakkala, Narangamuwa and Ranamure.
An indoor sports arena was discussed during a review of planned Kattankudy development works.
Consumer Affairs Authority continued special New Year inspections and investigations through April 30.
Nationwide festival food inspections continued, with legal action against 817 outlets.
Police conducted nationwide anti-drug operations under the national campaign, arresting 847 people.
Officials agreed to survey land parcels before considering their return to 17 owners.
Health Ministry issued appointment letters to 154 personnel across four professional categories.
The President's Secretary lodged a complaint seeking investigation of coal imports since 2009.
Officials decided to prioritize local councils for sand permits and organize local-authority distribution.
Navy opened its 1,153rd reverse-osmosis water purification station at Anuradhapura District Secretariat.
Kilinochchi district meeting decided to start a new sand supply system and halve prices.
Government announced a committee to investigate 462 coal shipments imported since 2010.
Government allocated funds for a one-time additional fertilizer subsidy for small tea growers.
The government decided to establish a presidential commission to investigate coal-related issues.
Officials planned extra surveillance cameras and security measures at Pettah Central Bus Station.
IMF and Sri Lanka reached staff-level agreement on the fifth and sixth EFF reviews.
Cyclone-damaged Northern Railway line repairs completed and Colombo–Kankesanthurai services restarted.
Colombo Fort Railway Station passenger-facility upgrade launched with ADB and government funding.
President announced a fuel subsidy of 50 rupees per litre for fishers.
District committee set water-sharing terms and cultivation plans for 2,409 acres.
Purchase orders were issued to speed fertilizer distribution for the cultivation season.
Northern Province decided to develop a business policy and appointed three planning committees.
Renovated Colombo Central Bus Station handed over for public use.
Prime Minister directed officials to expedite cyclone-damaged home repairs and new construction.
President said further northern lands would be gradually released and directed officials to examine next steps.
Transport Commission arranged extra holiday services, including 800 additional daily private-bus trips.
Officials appointed a committee to examine an alternative waste disposal site in Vavuniya.
President announced 100 billion rupees in three-month relief for people and industries affected by the Middle East conflict.
Treasury fuel subsidies of 100 rupees per diesel litre and 20 per petrol litre were set for three months.
Ordinary fishing boats will receive 31,250 rupees for 625 litres monthly, while multi-day boats receive 150,000 rupees.
Government allocated 6.5 billion rupees for fertilizer subsidies and increased several support rates.
Fertilizer support for other crops rises to 18,000 rupees per hectare.
Government allocated 8.5 billion rupees to increase Aswesuma payments for this month.
Radiotherapy services stopped after the hospital's linear accelerator broke down on March 31.
Cabinet approved a new economic relief package for the public.
Cabinet approved a fuel subsidy of 50 rupees per litre for small boats.
Railway Department planned to resume daily Northern Line services from April 9.
The final 2024 population and housing census report was formally handed to the President.
Government launched the National QR Payment Incentive Programme.
The programme committee approved a five-part communications and promotion plan.
Government cancelled the weekly Wednesday special holiday arrangement.
SLTB launched a refurbished safari bus for tourism services.
Development work began to modernise the Hatton SLTB depot.
World Bank-funded Veerasingam anicut construction was completed.
President said targeted diesel buyers would receive a subsidy of up to Rs. 100.
Government began high-level talks with Russia about purchasing coal for Norochcholai power plant.
Officials said ten low-floor buses would begin operating on two routes from April.
Officials said a dedicated accessible information website for persons with disabilities would be created.
Budget allocated Rs. 50 million for education access for low-income children with disabilities.
Budget allocated Rs. 864 million to improve lives of disabled armed forces and police personnel.
Budget allocated Rs. 80 million for vocational training for people with disabilities aged 16–35.
Rs. 17.4 million allocated for scholarships and assistive devices for visually impaired university students.
Budget allocated Rs. 5.75 million to continue disability employment measures in 2026.
Officials said a ten-year national health policy would be published the following April.
Police conducted nationwide anti-drug operations under the national campaign.
Water supply interruptions in several Colombo-area locations were shortened.
A new office for the 1990 Suwasariya emergency medical service opened in Colombo.
MP allocated 1.2 million rupees for a paddy drying floor in Olumadu.
Water board decided to reduce planned supply interruptions to 18 hours.
Cabinet set government fuel allowances using March 1 prices amid spending controls.
Agriculture service centres opened on holidays to maintain fertilizer distribution to farmers.
President directed officials to organize fertilizer distribution and consider alternative imports.
Cabinet set March 1 fuel prices as the basis for officials’ fuel allowances.
Water Board decided to restrict continuous water supply in drought-affected areas.
Ministries reported ongoing fuel and energy management measures, including diesel savings.
School-level energy management awareness sessions were planned for April 7 and 9.
Officials began raids against fertilizer stockpiling across Anuradhapura District.
Officials said seized fertilizer would be distributed to farmers through agrarian service centres.
Parliamentary committee directed Finance Ministry to prepare a tax mechanism for illicit beedi leaf imports.
Health Ministry launched national guidelines standardising oxygen use in government hospitals.
UNICEF supported launch of national oxygen-use guidelines for government hospitals.
Water supply was scheduled for rotating 24-hour cuts in several areas due to drought.
Alcohol bottle security sticker scheme officially launched to improve tax collection.
Contract awarded to Madras Security Printers; 1,000 stickers cost US$5.99.
Odd-even QR fuel distribution resumed for several weeks to prevent queues.
Minister proposed a national kidney stone surgery referral centre at Meerigama Hospital.
Justice Ministry launched a management system and modernized public services website.
